title: Which Groups Are Safe?
intro: A secure eye depends on the stones around it. Compare a group with two eyes and a gap that only looks like an eye.

steps.instruction: You are White. Try placing a stone in either empty eye.
steps.hint: Play in one of the eyes. The game will stop you.
steps.explanation: The move is refused. It captures nothing because Black still has the other eye, and White would have no liberty.

steps.instruction: You are White. Try playing in Black's apparent eye.
steps.hint: One of the three stones around that eye is not attached to the others, and it is standing on one liberty.
steps.explanation: The move captures a black stone at the boundary. That capture makes the move legal.

steps.instruction: The loose stone is now connected. Try the White move again.
steps.hint: Play the eye. The game will stop you.
steps.explanation: No black stones are captured this time. White would have no liberty, so the move is refused.

outro: The boundary matters. A group can live without already having two eyes; these examples show why counting eyes alone is not a test for every position.
